eyebrow: Data Governance Career & Capstone · Chapter One
titlePlain: Creating Data Quality Rules and SQL
subtitle: Lesson 7 · SQL Data Quality Checks

code:
-- RULE: ORD-001 — OrderTotal must be positive
SELECT OrderId, CustomerId, OrderTotal
FROM dbo.Orders
WHERE OrderTotal <= 0
ORDER BY OrderTotal ASC;
caption: Owned by steward Sam Okonjo — a zero or negative total means a failed calculation or an unvoided cancellation.

eyebrow: Rule 2 — Email must be present and well-formed
code:
-- RULE: CUST-001 — Email must be present and well-formed
SELECT CustomerId, Email
FROM dbo.Customers
WHERE Email IS NULL
   OR Email NOT LIKE '%_@_%._%';
caption: Owned by steward Priya Anand — ties directly back to Lesson 1's access-request gap.

code:
-- RULE: PROD-001 — SKU must be unique
SELECT SKU, COUNT(*) AS RecordCount
FROM dbo.Products
GROUP BY SKU
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
caption: Owned by steward Diego Marsh — enforces Lesson 5's "SKUs are never reused" rule.

code:
-- RULE: ORD-002 — every OrderLine must belong to a real Order
SELECT ol.OrderLineId, ol.OrderId
FROM dbo.OrderLines AS ol
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM dbo.Orders AS o
    WHERE o.OrderId = ol.OrderId
);
caption: An orphaned line quietly breaks any report that joins Orders to OrderLines.

code:
SELECT 'ORD-001: OrderTotal must be positive' AS RuleName,
       CAST(OrderId AS VARCHAR(20)) AS RecordKey
FROM dbo.Orders WHERE OrderTotal <= 0
UNION ALL
SELECT 'CUST-001: Email must be present and well-formed',
       CAST(CustomerId AS VARCHAR(20))
FROM dbo.Customers
WHERE Email IS NULL OR Email NOT LIKE '%_@_%._%';
caption: The first two branches of the failures report — same RuleName and RecordKey shape.

code:
SELECT 'PROD-001: SKU must be unique', SKU
FROM dbo.Products GROUP BY SKU HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
UNION ALL
SELECT 'ORD-002: OrderLine must belong to a real Order',
       CAST(ol.OrderLineId AS VARCHAR(20))
FROM dbo.OrderLines AS ol
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM dbo.Orders AS o WHERE o.OrderId = ol.OrderId
);
caption: Appended to part 1 with another UNION ALL — one row per violation, labeled by rule.
